newsitem.title: USA: U.S. might consider more food aid for N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. might consider more food aid for N.Korea.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said on Monday it would consider further food aid to famine-stricken North Korea if this were requested by the U.N. World Food Programme.

"If the World Food Programme comes forward again and says: 'It's not enough from the international comunity. We need more', we would obviously look at that very seriously," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

The United States has already responded twice this year to WFP appeals for food for North Korea, making contributions of $10 million and $15 million. "This may not be the end of the story," Burns told a news briefing.

Burns admitted that North Korean officials had raised the issue of food aid throughout a series of meetings they have held with U.S. and South Korean officials in New York since Wednesday on a proposal for talks on a permanent Korean peace.

North Korea has so far not given a definitive response to the U.S.-South Korean proposal for four-party talks involving the two Koreas, the United States and China. It remains unclear how the meetings in New York will end.

"Our view is we are responding adequately and vigorously and with some compassion from the humanitarian point of view to the desperate food situation of the North Koreans...but let's not link food aid or any other issues as preconditions or conditions to the four-party talks proposal," Burns said.
